title: Pathway Rotation: AI Prompt Engineering & Automation
description: Week 4 is the AI Prompt Engineering rotation, where every AI skill learned is applied to the participant's live pipeline the same day. They practice structured prompting across Claude and ChatGPT, comparing model outputs and judging fitness for purpose; accelerate research and personalization with AI while critiquing AI drafts for accuracy and authenticity; and design and build a working automation that saves measurable time in their own workflow. Weekly milestone: one working automation demoed to the cohort with a time-saved estimate.
notes: Weekly milestone: one working automation demoed to the cohort with a time-saved estimate.
lesson_length: Lab-guide lessons, roughly 1200-1800 words each, supporting a full week of live instructor-led practice
learning_objectives: Prompt Claude and ChatGPT with structure, comparing outputs and judging fitness for purpose
Use AI to accelerate research and personalization while critiquing drafts for accuracy and authenticity
Design and build a working automation with a measurable time-saved estimate

lessons.title: Working with LLMs
objectives: Prompt Claude and ChatGPT with structure, comparing outputs and judging fitness for purpose

lessons.title: AI-Assisted Prospecting
objectives: Use AI to accelerate research and personalization while critiquing drafts for accuracy and authenticity
Catch fabricated details and generic filler in AI drafts before sending

lessons.title: Build an Automation
objectives: Design and build a working automation with a measurable time-saved estimate
Select an automation candidate by frequency, time cost, and repeatability

sequencing_rationale: Week 4 is the AI Prompt Engineering rotation; every skill is applied to the live pipeline the same day. Structured prompting first (foundation), AI-assisted prospecting second (applies prompting to research and personalization with accuracy critique), the automation build last as the week's project deliverable demoed to the cohort. Scope assumption: Claude and ChatGPT are named because the program names them; automation tooling stays vendor-neutral.
